A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 20-page versions of Oscillatory State-Space Models. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original LinOSS classification, regression and forecasting results in Tables 1–3, plus ablations and harmonic-motion simulation results in Appendix C.

after.justification: V3 retains the original LinOSS experiments in Tables 1–3 and the ablation and simulation outcomes in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The oscillatory dynamics, IM and IMEX discretizations, parallel scans and full architecture in Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Appendix D's higher-order LinOSS-VV formulation is also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six UEA classification datasets, PPG-DaLiA heart-rate regression, weather forecasting and synthetic harmonic-motion prediction. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds NCDE to the PPG-DaLiA comparison, although NCDE already appeared in the UEA experiments. Table 3 removes the Informer† comparator while retaining ordinary Informer. Other comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported splits, preprocessing, sequence lengths, metrics, forecasting horizon and hyperparameter-search procedures remain unchanged, including Appendix B's selected configurations. The PDFs do not document a protocol revision explaining the replaced baseline scores.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 and Appendix C retain the same parameterization, initialization, timestep-sensitivity and dissipative-versus-conservative analyses. LinOSS ablation results and Figures 2–3 are unchanged; Table 6 only updates the accompanying baseline results.

E5.justification: Five-run reporting, random-initialization and split information, and the existing uncertainty-reporting practices are retained. Changed numerical standard deviations accompany revised results without a stated change to run counts or statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 6 replace results for NRDE, NCDE, Log-NCDE, LRU and S5. S5's average accuracy changes from 63.1% to 61.8%, but it overtakes LinOSS-IM on SCP1 with 89.9% versus 87.8%. In Table 2's MSE×10^-2 units, NRDE changes from 18.79 to 9.90 and LRU from 15.64 to 12.17; Log-NCDE and S5 also change. NCDE's 13.54 result is added, while Table 3 loses Informer†'s 0.741 MAE. LinOSS's own scores remain unchanged, but comparative rankings and margins are substantially revised.

T1.justification: The stability propositions, universality theorem, mathematical assumptions and derivations are unchanged, including the higher-order integration formulas and proofs in Appendices D–E.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the claimed advantage over LRU on the roughly 50k-step task from 2.5× to nearly 2×, matching revised Table 2. The central contributions concerning oscillatory models, stability, universality, time reversibility and long-sequence modeling remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same interpretations of dissipation, conservation, initialization sensitivity and timestep effects. Appendix E's qualification concerning exploding gradients when learning chaotic systems is also unchanged.

D1.justification: Architecture details, JAX implementation, GPU hardware, hyperparameter searches, selected settings and resource measurements remain unchanged in Appendices A–B. The code repository is the same; its introductory wording is merely shortened.

R1.justification: V3 adds Kidger et al. (2020), Neural Controlled Differential Equations for Irregular Time Series, as the citation for NCDE in Table 2 and in the references. Section 2.2's research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits are localized to performance summaries, the shortened code statement and citation formatting. Section 4.1 removes the explicit 85%-to-95% EigenWorms comparison. The overall narrative, section order and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 2 and 3 respectively gain and lose a comparator row, while Tables 1 and 6 swap the S6 and Mamba row order. Minor spacing and page-flow changes reposition existing material, including Figure 1; the figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: V3 modestly broadens Table 2 with NCDE and its attribution, but removes the Informer† comparison from Table 3. The dominant changes replace baseline scores in Tables 1, 2 and 6 without explaining why the earlier values were superseded. Both versions align their performance summaries with their respective tables, and LinOSS's method and own scores are unchanged. The PDFs therefore do not establish whether the revisions produce a net improvement in reliability or overall quality.
